knowledge_graph.title: Hib vaccine
knowledge_graph.description: The Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccine, also known as Hib vaccine, is a vaccine used to prevent Haemophilus influenzae type b infection. In countries that include it as a routine vaccine, rates of severe Hib infections have decreased more than 90%.

text_blocks.snippet: The Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine is a safe and effective way to protect against serious Hib disease, which can cause meningitis, pneumonia, and other severe illnesses, particularly in young children. The vaccine is typically given to infants as part of their routine childhood immunization schedule.
snippet_highlighted_words: a safe and effective way to protect against serious Hib disease, which can cause meningitis, pneumonia, and other severe illnesses, particularly in young children

text_blocks.snippet: Hib is a type of bacteria that can cause a range of illnesses, from mild ear infections to severe, life-threatening infections like meningitis and pneumonia. Before the vaccine, Hib was a leading cause of bacterial meningitis in children under 5. Meningitis, an infection of the brain and spinal cord lining, can lead to brain damage, deafness, and even death.
